executive_summary: This chapter explores Factors, Multiples, Highest Common Factor (HCF / GCD), and Least Common Multiple (LCM) through practical real-world problems such as finding maximum square tile dimensions to fit a room without cutting, or finding the shortest common length for cloth torans. It establishes prime factorisation as a structured method to find HCF (by taking the product of common prime factors with the smallest powers) and LCM (by taking the product of all prime factors with their highest powers). The relationship between HCF, LCM, and number products is also investigated.
key_takeaways: Factor: A number that divides another number completely leaving remainder 0.
Multiple: The product of a given number and any integer.
Co-prime Numbers: Two numbers whose HCF is 1.
HCF-LCM Relation Formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
